basis: Cutaneous papular disease of uncertain etiology; inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: proposed immune mechanisms remain uncertain; the supplied definition establishes cutaneous disease without a confirmed immune mechanism.

basis: Skeletal dwarfism with insulin resistance and dyslipidemia; hepatic steatosis 2/2 and retinal detachment 1/2. Microcephaly alone does not demonstrate neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly lacks accompanying evidence of brain dysfunction or developmental impairment in this subtype.
decisions.ocular: involved: retinal detachment directly damages the eye and affects 1/2 reported patients; the small cohort limits certainty.

basis: Immunodeficiency and subcutaneous fat loss define disease; hypothyroidism 3/4; severe developmental delay 4/5. Ocular malformations 5/5 and thrombocytopenia 4/5 omitted at cap.

decisions.haematologic: none after cap: thrombocytopenia affects 4/5, but defining axes and severe developmental impairment take priority.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: defining lipodystrophy directly affects subcutis; complete absence of subcutaneous fat occurs in 5/5.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia defines disease. Dental crowding 12/15 lacks demonstrated damage or dysfunction; enamel hypoplasia 4/15 is below 30%. Cardiac and developmental abnormalities are uncommon.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: crowding in 12/15 does not establish damaged teeth or impaired oral function; enamel hypoplasia occurs in 4/15, below 30%.

basis: Spastic ataxia caused by impaired coenzyme Q biosynthesis; visual impairment in 1/3 is not localized to ocular structures.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment occurs in 1/3 assessed patients, but ocular injury is not established and central visual dysfunction remains possible.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this COQ4-associated ataxia results from defective coenzyme Q biosynthesis, an inborn metabolic mechanism.

basis: Primary hepatic malignancy; portal venous invasion with tumor thrombosis directly occupies vessels. Portal vein thrombosis is frequent (30–79%) in the supplied HPO annotations.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: HCC directly invades portal veins and produces tumor thrombus; supplied HPO places portal vein thrombosis at 30–79%.

basis: Infantile autophagic vacuolar skeletal myopathy; cardiomyopathy is reported without an established frequency or diagnostic requirement. Developmental delay may reflect muscle weakness.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is reported, but the evidence does not establish occurrence in at least 30% or status as a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Cerebellar dysfunction, intellectual disability and gonadotropin deficiency define disease; scoliosis 3/3 and strabismus 1/3 support additional involvement. Small cohort.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus represents ocular alignment dysfunction in 1/3 reported patients, meeting the supplied frequency threshold.

basis: Single-patient evidence: alveolar hemorrhage/respiratory failure, endocrine autoimmunity and marrow hypocellularity each 1/1. Arthritis 1/1 omitted at cap.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: diabetes with anti-insulin antibodies and hypothyroidism occur in 1/1; endocrine autoimmunity is a direct manifestation of this immune dysregulation syndrome.

basis: Myopathy with defining ocular dysfunction: ptosis 24/24 and external ophthalmoplegia 14/20. Dysphagia reflects swallowing-muscle weakness without established gastrointestinal injury.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular dysfunction is a defining component of oculopharyngodistal myopathy, with ptosis in 24/24 and ophthalmoplegia in 14/20.
